# Status report — query-once-per-tick + decide-and-fix-not-decide-and-ask: real code already built, real gap found and fixed on its own PR

UMR chain: addendum to UMR-20260813-102459-10c3 (chain: 084321-2962 ->
102459-10c3 -> this addendum -> P1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767). Governing
UMR for this task: `UMR-20260813-105106-e9a7`.

## Verdict

**Both Owner directives were already built as real, runtime-enforced code
in `pm-sentinel-tick.sh` on `FChecklist/veridian-scripts#299` by a prior
invocation of this exact UMR** (that invocation's own worker unit went
`ActiveState=inactive` with an ambiguous `task.yaml` checkpoint, which is
why the platform re-queued this UMR as a fresh task — see
`resource_governor.py --query-umr --umr-id UMR-20260813-105106-e9a7`,
`reason` field). Independently re-verifying that PR from a **fresh clone**
(not this box's live checkout, not trusted from the prior self-report)
found one real, concrete gap — PR #299 was missing the two systemd unit
files its own script docstring assumes exist — which is fixed here, on
that same PR, with the fix pushed and PR #298 (the now-fully-superseded
predecessor) closed to keep exactly one live PR for this file.

## Part 1 — what was already real (independently re-verified, not trusted)

`FChecklist/veridian-scripts#299` (`pm-sentinel-tick.sh`, single squashed
commit `9e3469f`, base = current `main`, `mergeable=MERGEABLE`,
`mergeStateStatus=CLEAN`) contains both directives as real code, not
narration:

1. **QUERY ONCE PER TICK** — `get_umr_row()` / `cache_put_row()` /
   `already_queried_this_tick()`, a real **on-disk** per-tick cache
   (`CACHE_DIR="$(mktemp -d ...)"`, `trap 'rm -rf "$CACHE_DIR"' EXIT`) —
   deliberately not a bash associative array, because every call site
   invokes these functions via `$(...)` command substitution, which bash
   always forks a subshell for; an in-memory `declare -A` write there would
   be silently lost the instant the subshell exits. The script's own header
   comment documents this as a real bug the test itself caught during
   development. Every bulk listing query (killed-row scan, running-row
   cross-check, `completed_unmerged` PR audit) populates the same cache via
   `cache_put_row()`; every per-row loop calls
   `already_queried_this_tick()` first and skips a row a prior check this
   same tick already fetched+handled. `cached_gh_pr_view` does the same for
   `gh pr view` / `gh api .../comments` calls, keyed by `(repo, pr_number)`.
2. **DECIDE-AND-FIX, NOT DECIDE-AND-ASK** — every real gap-detection call
   site calls `record_finding()` immediately before `dispatch_gap()`
   (`FINDINGS_LOGGED`); `dispatch_gap()` — the one real gateway every
   finding must go through, itself calling `dispatch-owner-task.sh
   --no-relay`, the same single front door `resource_governor.py`'s
   tier/concurrency-cap/`EMERGENCY_STOP`/stop-work gate already sits behind
   — increments `FINDINGS_ACTIONED` on every one of its own real terminal
   outcomes (dispatched, dispatch attempted-but-failed, already in-flight,
   per-tick cap reached, genuine financial escalation). At tick end, if
   `FINDINGS_LOGGED != FINDINGS_ACTIONED` the tick fails loudly
   (`DECIDE-AND-FIX VIOLATION`, non-zero exit) instead of silently leaving a
   finding undecided.

Real test evidence, re-run independently in a throwaway clone
(`/tmp/vs-review`, not this box's live checkout) rather than trusted from
the prior invocation's own report:

```
$ python3 -m pytest test_pm_sentinel_tick.py -v
PmSentinelTickKilledRowTest::test_first_tick_dispatches_real_rca_for_seeded_killed_row PASSED
PmSentinelTickKilledRowTest::test_second_tick_does_not_duplicate_already_in_flight_dispatch PASSED
PmSentinelTickFinancialEscalationTest::test_financial_gap_escalates_to_owner_instead_of_dispatching PASSED
PmSentinelTickDispatchFailurePropagatesTest::test_real_dispatch_failure_makes_tick_exit_nonzero PASSED
PmSentinelTickQueryOncePerTickTest::test_same_row_queried_at_most_once_per_tick PASSED
PmSentinelTickDecideAndFixTest::test_every_finding_gets_a_same_tick_dispatch PASSED
6 passed in 291.89s
```

`PmSentinelTickQueryOncePerTickTest` seeds one real `umr_id` that is
*both* a tracked-chain head *and* `status='killed'` — the concrete overlap
case where, pre-addendum, Check 1 and Check 2a would each independently
issue their own real `resource_governor.py --query-umr --umr-id <same id>`
call for the identical row — and asserts, via a real logging shim that
execs the real `resource_governor.py` (so real tick behavior is completely
unchanged), that the id is queried exactly once. `PmSentinelTickDecideAndFixTest`
seeds two independent real gaps and asserts each gets its own real
`dispatch-owner-task.sh` call in the same tick, with
`FINDINGS_LOGGED`/`FINDINGS_ACTIONED` reconciling and no
`DECIDE-AND-FIX VIOLATION`.

## Part 2 — the real gap found on independent review, and the fix

`claude-control#143`'s own audit (posted 2026-08-13T13:08:44Z, before this
task's re-dispatch) correctly flagged that a documentation-only PR in this
repo cannot substitute for an independent review of the actual code in
`veridian-scripts#299`, and that #299 needed that review before merge. This
task supplies that review, in a fresh clone rather than the live checkout:

- `git diff main pr299 --stat` on a clean clone showed exactly two files:
  `pm-sentinel-tick.sh` (922 new lines) and `test_pm_sentinel_tick.py` (587
  new lines) — **no `systemd/` files**, even though the script's own header
  comment says it is "wired as a systemd --user timer (see
  `systemd/veridian-pm-sentinel-tick.service` + `.timer` in this same
  directory)". Those two files were real and already present on the prior,
  now-superseded `#298` (`git diff pr298 pr299 --stat` confirmed the delta),
  and already live+active on this box
  (`systemctl --user show veridian-pm-sentinel-tick.timer -p ActiveState`:
  `active`) — they were simply dropped when `#299`'s squash commit carried
  the script and tests forward from `#298` but not the systemd units.
- Fixed on `#299` itself (commit `5e3eeeb`, pushed to
  `worker/task-20260813-123933-add-query-once-decide-and-fix`): restored
  both files, verified **byte-identical** (`diff`, zero delta) to both
  `#298`'s versions and the live, active deployment — not new/invented
  content, real already-authored content this PR should have carried
  forward.
- Re-ran the full real test suite against the fixed branch: 6/6 pass
  (unchanged from Part 1 — the fix only added previously-missing files, it
  did not touch `pm-sentinel-tick.sh` or the tests).
- `#298` (`feat: collapse server-native PM sentinel + financial-escalation
  + hierarchy policy into ONE script (10c3)`) closed as superseded — `#299`
  is now a strict superset (script + tests + systemd units + the
  query-once/decide-and-fix addendum), so keeping both open would itself be
  the duplication this UMR chain's own zero-duplication rule forbids.
- `claude-control#143` (the doc-only status report this audit-failed)
  closed rather than rebased — its `STATUS_REPORT.md`-only branch had
  diverged through five more merges to `master` since it was cut
  (`#144`/`#145`/`#148`), and this report supersedes it directly rather
  than mechanically replaying a stale rebase.

Not done here, out of this task's own scope: actually merging `#299` into
`veridian-scripts:main` — this platform's own convention is that workers
open PRs and a separate audit/merge step lands them (see `dispatch-tick`'s
own `completed_unmerged` PR-audit path, which `pm-sentinel-tick.sh` itself
reuses rather than reimplements); `#299` is now real, tested, and
`mergeable=CLEAN` and ready for that step.

## Completed

- [x] Independently re-verified (fresh clone, not the live checkout or the
      prior invocation's self-report) that both Owner directives
      (query-once-per-tick, decide-and-fix-not-decide-and-ask) are real,
      runtime-enforced code in `pm-sentinel-tick.sh` on
      `veridian-scripts#299`.
- [x] Independently re-ran the full real test suite (6/6 pass), including
      the two tests specific to this addendum
      (`PmSentinelTickQueryOncePerTickTest`,
      `PmSentinelTickDecideAndFixTest`).
- [x] Found a real gap on independent review: `#299` was missing the
      systemd unit files its own script assumes exist.
- [x] Fixed the gap on `#299` itself (commit `5e3eeeb`), byte-identical to
      the already-live deployment; re-verified 6/6 tests still pass.
- [x] Closed `#298` as superseded (now redundant with the fixed `#299`).
- [x] Closed `#143` (stale, audit-failed, superseded by this report).

## Remaining

- [ ] `veridian-scripts#299` itself still needs the platform's own
      independent merge/audit step (out of a worker's own authority —
      workers do not merge/push-main on this platform) before it lands on
      `main`.

repo. That was wrong: `claude-control`'s `scripts/` directory has been

body:
Owner-requested (2026-07-27): script that dedupes ai-os/tasks/*/task.yaml repeat-attempt chains into distinct issues, checks real GitHub PR state, and writes a JSON+Markdown completion plan.

## Update (2026-07-27): root-cause fix for a confirmed mass-mislabeling incident

**This PR was never merged**, and the script it adds has always been read-only (it only ever wrote `ai-os/BACKLOG_COMPLETION_PLAN_2026-07-27.{json,md}`, never any `task.yaml`). Despite that, on 2026-07-27, 32 real `ai-os/tasks/*/task.yaml` files were hand-edited to `status=superseded` with `superseded_reason` text falsely citing "Collapsed by plan_backlog_completion.py dedup 2026-07-27" -- attributing an automated collapse decision to a tool that never made one and never had a write path at all. Cross-checking all 32 against this same plan run's own JSON classification shows only 2 of 32 had a category that even arguably means "already done" (`ALREADY_DONE_STALE_STATUS`); the other 30 were `PR_PENDING_MERGE`, `PR_CLOSED_NEEDS_REDISPATCH`, `SUBSTANTIAL_WORK_NO_PR_NEEDS_REVIEW`, or `OWNER_OR_REVIEWER_DECISION_NEEDED` -- none of which mean "collapse, work is done."

This update closes both gaps that made that incident possible:

### 1. Real-verification gap in `classify()`
Before concluding `ALREADY_DONE_STALE_STATUS` for an issue, `classify()` now:
- Finds the group's real original (non-`rca-`) task via `find_group_original()`.
- Parses its `SUCCESS_CRITERIA` from `prompt.txt` using `tight_task_validation.py`'s existing `parse_labeled_fields()` (reused, not reimplemented).
- Extracts mechanically-runnable `pytest`/`grep` invocations (`extract_verifiable_commands()`).
- Actually re-runs them against a fresh, isolated clone of the repo's real current default branch (`get_repo_checkout()` / `verify_success_criteria()`) -- not just a regex scan of checkpoint prose for a PR-number mention.
- Only concludes `ALREADY_DONE_STALE_STATUS` if that re-run actually passes. If it doesn't, the new category is `PR_MERGED_BUT_SUCCESS_CRITERIA_UNVERIFIED` (do not collapse -- needs Owner/reviewer decision). If `SUCCESS_CRITERIA` is prose-only/missing, the new category is `CANNOT_AUTO_VERIFY_NEEDS_HUMAN_READ` -- never silently treated as verified.

### 2. Missing real apply mechanism
There was previously no auditable code path that could ever write a collapse to `task.yaml` -- which is exactly how the incident happened (an unaudited hand-edit). Added:
- `apply_collapse()` + `--apply` CLI flag: the **only** code path in this repo allowed to write `status=superseded`/`duplicate_of`/`superseded_reason` to a real `task.yaml`. Refuses any category other than this run's own verified `ALREADY_DONE_STALE_STATUS`, and refuses to write without a cited evidence string (real checked commit/PR -- never a generic "same underlying issue" claim).
- `--audit-report` read-only mode: cross-checks every real `task.yaml` already marked `status=superseded` with a `superseded_reason` citing this routine against what the fixed classifier concludes *today*, and writes mismatches to a report artifact. Never writes to `task.yaml`.

### 3. Regression tests
`tests/plan_backlog_completion_dedup_test.py` (9 tests, synthetic fixtures under `tests/fixtures/dedup_083946_incident/` and `tests/fixtures/dedup_prose_only_criteria/` -- no real `ai-os/tasks/` data touched) reproduces the real historical fixture: `task-20260726-083946` (original), its rca-chain retries, PR #81 (closed without merging), and PR #104 (real, merged, but its actual diff only fixes an unrelated crontab preflight hard-stop, not branch resolution or hold-for-signoff). Asserts the fixed logic does **not** credit PR #104's merge with satisfying the original `SUCCESS_CRITERIA`, and does not silently produce a collapse-eligible category on lineage/chain-length alone.

```
python3 -m pytest tests/ -k "dedup" -v
# 9 passed
python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
# 94 passed (full suite, no regressions)
```

### 4. Real, non-mutating audit run
`ai-os/DEDUP_MISMATCH_MANUAL_REVIEW_2026-07-27.yaml` is a real `--audit-report` run against the live `ai-os/tasks/` tree: **31 of the 32** real superseded records citing this routine do not actually qualify as `ALREADY_DONE_STALE_STATUS` under the fixed classifier (one more than the ~30 estimated -- `task-20260726-171157` was previously counted "OK" only because the old naive check trusted a merged-PR mention with zero `SUCCESS_CRITERIA` verification; its `SUCCESS_CRITERIA` turns out to be prose-only, so the fixed logic correctly downgrades it to `CANNOT_AUTO_VERIFY_NEEDS_HUMAN_READ` rather than silently trusting it either).

**Proof of zero mutation**: md5 hashes of all 522 real `ai-os/tasks/*/task.yaml` files were taken immediately before and after this `--audit-report` run. Zero changes among the 32 records this run processed. (5 unrelated files changed during the run window -- other live workers on this server concurrently checkpointing their own in-progress, unrelated tasks; none are among the 32 targets.)

Per this task's own constraints, `--apply` was **not** invoked against any real record during this work -- the report above is for Owner manual review only. `apply_collapse()`'s write behavior is exercised only against isolated test fixtures.

## EXPECTED_OUTPUT / CONSTRAINTS

`HOLD_FOR_OWNER_SIGNOFF: true`

This touches the integrity of real task-tracking records at scale (30+ existing records potentially affected by the original incident). Do not auto-merge -- hold for explicit Owner review of `ai-os/DEDUP_MISMATCH_MANUAL_REVIEW_2026-07-27.yaml` and this diff.

body:
## Why a new PR instead of continuing PR #80

This task (task-20260726-171226) was dispatched to fix a round-4 audit
finding (`AUDIT: REJECT`) on PR #80's branch
(`worker/task-20260726-083833-build-interactive-session-write-gate--re`),
which was open at round-4 commit `353fa09` when this task started. While
this fix was being built and tested, **PR #80 merged into `master`**
(merge commit `ec95532`, at `2026-07-26T17:18:34Z`) — carrying the
round-4 code, which still has the alias bypass described below, into
`master` unpatched. A merged PR cannot be reopened to carry new commits
through review, so this is a new PR from the same branch (now containing
both what merged as PR #80 and this round's fix on top) targeting
`master`, per the same "open a PR, leave the merge to the real pipeline"
discipline every prior round of this effort has followed. **This PR is
not merged by this task** — that is left to the real review/dispatch
pipeline, consistent with the article this guard itself exists to
enforce (`PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml` A8/A15).

## What this fixes

A fresh audit of round 4, verified by direct live reproduction (not just
review), found that native git/gh command **aliasing** was a total,
undetected bypass of the interactive-session write gate
(`ai-os/OWNER_DIRECTIVES/interactive-session-guard.bashrc-snippet`):

- `git -c alias.<name>=push <name> <remote> <branch>` — a one-shot alias
  defined on the command line itself — reproduced live against a real
  git 2.43 install: this really pushes, with zero trace in
  `~/.gitconfig`. A pre-existing `[alias]` entry in `~/.gitconfig` (e.g.
  `alias.wip = push`, then `git wip origin master`) behaves identically.
- `gh alias set <name> 'pr merge ...'` then `gh <name> ...` — the same
  class for gh, reproduced live against a real gh 2.45 install.

No prior round's subcommand-detection logic had an alias-resolution
step at all, so an alias name that wasn't literally `push`/`pr merge`
walked straight past detection while the real git/gh binary still
expanded and ran it.

### Fix

- **One-shot** `-c alias.*=` / `--config-env alias.*=...` command-line
  aliases are **rejected outright**, unconditionally — a legitimate
  dispatch-pipeline invocation has no reason to define one inline, and
  the value could itself be a shell alias or something else unsafe to
  statically evaluate.
- **Persistent** `~/.gitconfig` `[alias]` / `gh alias set` entries are
  **resolved one level** by asking the real git/gh binary what it
  actually knows (`git config --get-regexp '^alias\.'` / `gh alias
  list`) before deciding a subcommand token isn't a guarded action.

Both bypasses are proven blocked by new regression-test scenarios that
reproduce the review's exact repro commands.

### Honestly disclosed residual gaps (found while building this fix)

- Alias resolution is only **one level deep** — a nested alias (alias A
  → alias B → push) isn't followed further.
- A gh **shell alias** (`!...`) is left unresolved by this guard's own
  logic (though often still incidentally caught in practice, because
  real gh's alias expansion re-invokes `gh` through the same
  guard-prepended `$PATH`).
- Persistent-alias values that use shell-style **quote-splicing or
  escaping** to spell out `master` (e.g. `push origin "ma""ster"`) are
  not recognized by this round's whitespace-only value split, since
  correctly and safely dequoting arbitrary alias text (without `eval`,
  which would execute attacker-influenced text as shell code) is out of
  scope for this round.

All three are covered by dedicated regression-test scenarios that
demonstrate the disclosed behavior, not silently passing or omitted.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash tests/interactive_session_guard_test.sh` — 82/82 scenarios
      pass (all pre-existing round 1-4 scenarios plus 15 new round-5
      scenarios), exit code 0.
- [x] Live-reproduced both bypasses from the review against real git
      2.43 / gh 2.45 installs before the fix, confirmed both are now
      blocked after the fix.
- [x] Verified the round-3/round-4 fixes (cgroup hardcoding, force-push
      refspec, multi-refspec, argv global-flag-position resolution) are
      unmodified and still pass all their existing scenarios.

- **phase_2** (`phase_2_compiler_pipeline_intelligence_engines`): amended objective + added a scope bullet naming Stage 4 Machine Prompt Builder / Prompt Compiler Engine (document line 79, "Natural language intent to optimized machine prompt via DSPy-style declarative compilation pipeline") as the real machine-language-output contract that both of phase_5's input surfaces must compile into. No new engine needed — the document's existing vocabulary already covers this.
- **phase_5** (`phase_5_browser_execution_tiers`): amended objective + added a scope bullet with three concrete deliverables (structured mode-pill/option-chain component, free-text chat component, browser-FIRST/server-SECOND handoff call), extended `integration_point` to cover the handoff via Gateway G05, and added a `success_criteria` item for a real end-to-end two-stage handoff command. Explicitly distinguished from the existing `engine-server-escalation` Tier-5 item, which is escalation-on-insufficiency only — the Owner's model is a *mandatory* second pass every time, not a fallback.

## Sourcing note (important finding)
Grepped the full extracted source document (`ai-os/owner-attachments/VERIDIAN_Architecture_v2.0_extracted.txt`, 564 lines) for "mode pill", "option chain", "chat input", "machine language" — **zero matches**. The premise that these are the document's own vocabulary does not hold; they are the Owner's own UX terminology from the chat clarification. Both amendments include an explicit "NOTE ON SOURCING" citing this, and instead anchor to the real closest document sections:
- Stage 1 "User Input" / Input Acquisition Layer (line 213-215) — the document's only abstract end-user input entry point.
- Prompt Compiler Engine, "Natural language intent to optimized machine prompt" (line 79) — the real machine-language-output contract.
- Stage 4 Machine Prompt Builder (line 225-227).
- Browser Execution Engine, "Master orchestrator for all browser-native execution" (line 144).
- Server Escalation Engine (line 179) — noted as a *different* concept (escalation-on-insufficiency) from the Owner's mandatory two-pass model.

- **phase_3** (governance/policy/cost): permission/audit/cost concerns apply identically regardless of which input surface or execution stage produced the request; no scope change needed.
